title: Upstream attempt
description: One upstream attempt and its reservation (architecture 7.4 to 7.6). An attempt exists only after its reservation transaction commits (B2), so every record starts in reserved with a ceiling. The allowed transitions are exactly those in $defs/transition (7.5); transitions lists the ones taken, in order. A reservation belongs to the windows it was made in, even if settlement happens after rollover (7.6). Ceilings and costs are integer nano-dollars; the ceiling is rounded up (6.4).

ceiling_nanodollars.description: The reservation ceiling (7.4), rounded up to the next nano-dollar. Null only for an unbounded request admitted under meter-only budgets, with ceiling_unavailable_reason (open question 3 in the PR).

budget_window_ids.description: The budget-window rows the reservation was made against, in ascending ID order, the order they were locked (7.6).

price_book_version.description: The price-book version effective when the reservation committed; this attempt is priced with it (P1).

retry_of_attempt_id.description: The attempt this relay retry repeats; null when it is not a retry. A retry is its own attempt with its own reservation (7.2).

transitions.description: Transitions taken, oldest first. Empty while the attempt is reserved.

release_reason.description: Why a reserved attempt was released: the upstream connection failed before any request byte was sent (7.5).

unknown_reason.description: Why the outcome is uncertain after dispatch (7.5).

allOf.$comment: The ceiling is null exactly when its reason is given.
unknown_reason stays on a record that later settled from unknown, as history; it is never set on one that did not pass through unknown.
A ceiling charge settles an unknown attempt at its full ceiling when no exact usage is found within the reconciliation window (7.5). It needs a ceiling to charge.

state.description: reserved: the reservation transaction committed; the ceiling is added to reserved on every applicable window. dispatched: the first byte was sent upstream. released: the upstream connection failed before any request byte was sent; the ceiling is released. settled: usage was obtained from the response or by reconciliation; the ceiling is released and the actual cost added to spent. unknown: the outcome is uncertain after dispatch; the ceiling stays reserved (7.5).

transition.description: One allowed state change (7.5). reserved to dispatched; reserved to released; dispatched to settled; dispatched to unknown; unknown to settled, when exact usage is found or the full ceiling is charged. released and settled are terminal. A relay crash between the reserve commit and the first byte is not covered yet (open question 1 in the PR).

transition_record.description: A transition taken, with when it happened.

allowed_pairs.$comment: The transition table as data (7.5), shared by transition and transition_record. Exactly one pair matches an allowed transition.

settlement.description: How a settled attempt's cost was established (7.5, 7.6). response_usage: usage in the response the relay handled. partial_stream_usage: exact usage found in partial stream events. provider_usage_by_request_id: provider usage data matched by request ID. ceiling_charge: no exact usage within the reconciliation window, so the full ceiling is charged. overrun is true when cost exceeded the ceiling, an invariant breach handled as an incident (7.6).
